summary: Isaac Schapera was an anthropologist and historian who studied at the University of Cape Town, Cándido Candi, and the London School of Economics. He held posts at the LSE (circa 1950–1972), the University of Toronto, and the University of Chicago.

Isaak Jakob Schmidt was a Tibetologist and scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, and Buddhist studies who earned his doctorate from the University of Rostock. He served the Russian Bible Society and held positions with the Imperial Academy of Sciences.

Isabelle Henrion-Dourcy is a Tibetologist who studied at Université libre de Bruxelles, Tibet University, EPHE, and Harvard, under Fernand Meyer and Françoise Lauwaert. She held posts at Laval University, where she taught anthropology around 2004.

Isabelle Ratié is an Indologist and philosopher who studied at Paris 1 and EPHE under Alexis Sanderson and Lyne Bansat-Boudon. She held posts at the Austrian Academy of Sciences, Leipzig, University of Paris, Sorbonne Nouvelle, and Collège de France.
Isaiah Berlin was a philosopher educated at St Paul's School and Corpus Christi College, Oxford. He spent his academic career holding a post at the University of Oxford from around 1932 to 1975.

Isaline Blew Horner was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at Newnham College and Cambridge under Caroline Rhys Davids. She held librarian and research posts at Newnham, Cambridge, and served as Honorary Secretary of the Pali Text Society.

Iselin Frydenlund is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. Her career includes attested appointments in 2016 as a senior researcher at the Peace Research Institute Oslo and as a research fellow at the University of Oslo.

Ishtiaq Hussain Qureshi was a historian and Indologist who studied at St. Stephen's College and Cambridge. He held posts at St. Stephen's, University of the Punjab, Columbia University, University of Karachi, and the National Language Promotion Department.

Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar was an Indologist, philosopher, and linguist educated at Sanskrit Collegiate School, Sanskrit College, and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University. He served at Fort William College, Sanskrit College, and became director of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University in 1851.

Iso Kern is a philosopher, Sinologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at UCLouvain, KU Leuven, Freiburg, Heidelberg, NTU, and Columbia. He taught at KU Leuven, Heidelberg, Zurich, Fribourg, and was named titular professor at the University of Bern.
Issai'en Ikeyama was a scholar in Buddhist studies. In 1976, he was attested as a professor at both Shitennoji Junior College and Eizan Gakuin.
Issei Suzuki was a scholar in Buddhist studies who was educated at Rissho University and subsequently held a post as a professor there.
Itsuko Nishikawa is a linguist and Japanologist who studied at Teachers College, Columbia University. She held a post at the University of Washington and taught Qian Lin.

Ivan Minayev was an Indologist, linguist, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Saint Petersburg State University. From circa 1869 to 1890, he held a post at the Faculty of Oriental Studies of Saint Petersburg University.

Ivan Pavlovich Minaev was an Indologist, linguist, and Buddhist studies scholar educated at Saint Petersburg State University under Vasily Pavlovich Vasilyev and Albrecht Weber. He served as a professor at Saint Petersburg State University.

Ives Goddard was a linguist who studied at Harvard College and Harvard University. He held an academic post at Harvard University (circa 1969–1976) and served at the Smithsonian Institution and National Museum of Natural History from around 1976 to 2025.
Ives Waldo is a scholar of philosophy, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at the University of Oxford and studied under Chögyam Trungpa from 1970 to 1988.

Ivette Vargas-O'Bryan is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who earned her PhD at Harvard under Leonard van der Kuijp, Charles Hallisey, Kurtis R. Schaeffer, and Theodore Riccardi Jr. She held a fellowship post at Grinnell College.

Ivo Fišer was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He held an appointment as a lecturer at Charles University, attested in 1960, and was attested in 1970 at the University of Copenhagen's Institute for Indian Philology.

Iwao Nakajima is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a master's degree from Hitotsubashi University and studied under Nikki Kimura. He worked at the NHK Broadcasting Culture Research Institute until 1975 and at Sandhaan around 1999.
